body:
I love the way this looks, compared to my original barebones UI for the warnings and errors!

There are a few things I've left comments on that I think would be good to address.
Most notably, I think the construction of each individual diagnostic item should be moved into its own Control-based class that you can create an instance of with `memnew` and populate with data using a method.

There was a rather strange bug I ran into while testing this PR, and it's possible it also existed in my original version. If I activate the tooltip with diagnostics, then try to select the diagnostic text and right-click it to get the context menu with copy/select all, sometimes the context menu will quickly disappear. The tooltip will then refuse to show up until I right-click text in the editor to make _its_ context menu show up, and dismiss it:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6aa5818b-6924-4da9-8183-2849cc9f02ea

The diagnostics should not be selectable at all, I must have missed it from the original PR.
The EditorHelpBitTooltip is implemented in a hacky way that should be improved first.
For instance, it is not possible to use keyboard shortcuts to copy selected text because of how it handles input. If selection is enabled then users would expect using the shortcut to copy to work.
- See https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/14271

This PR should just add icons and copy buttons, and disable the text selection.

Looking good! The `DiagnosticItemRow` class definition will need to get moved into a header file I'm pretty sure (could be `script_text_editor.h`, no need for a header file of its own necessarily), but I think this approach will work better.

With the new approach to the hover detection, multiple copy buttons aren't lighting up. However I do see that there is a way to seemingly make the copy button disappear, while the cursor is still over the diagnostic row:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/faec498b-e229-486a-9040-71c3cf8a6d13

If the appearing and disappearing button feature continues to give us grief, perhaps it would make sense to drop it and just have the button always be visible. That would simplify things on the programming side, as well as make it easier to notice (unless its appearing and disappearing causes people to notice it).

Really love the look of the new diagnostic hover tooltips. Though, there seems to be some tweaks still needed, especially in terms of margins. (I tried to take a screenshot, but the tooltip refused to show up again.) Also, it may be done in a future PR, but we should also update the warnings/error summary area at the bottom of the script view. --- I cannot really approve the PR at its current state. I really dislike the idea of passing a reference that can be freed on certain circumstances. Also, I saw that you replaced the idea of giving the `EditorHelpBitTooltip::make_tooltip` class multiple lines to instead giving the function a tooltip to integrate and modify. But it changes dramatically the way the method works. In master, the method is essentially a tool that you give some informations, and it takes care of everything. But here, you make it so that `make_tooltip` becomes dependent on each caller's implementations of their diagnostics. I would instead suggest instead to continue the way `EditorHelpBitTooltip::make_tooltip()` worked initially with `const String &p_diagnostics`, but instead of passing formatted strings, it could be a `const Vector &p_diagnostics` where `EditorHelpBitTooltip::DiagnosticEntry` is a struct that would describe a diagnostic entry (i.e. type, text (could be still rich, with url support and more), start line and column, end line and column). From there, the `make_tooltip()` will be able to create and shape the tooltip at it wants. Also, it will make the job way easier to make the diagnostics style uniform throughout the editor. So I'm suggesting to move your diagnostic classes from the script text editor file to the editor help one.

Tested again, and the hover behavior seems good to me! I wasn't able to trigger any cases where multiple buttons were visible, or all buttons disappeared (except when they should have, such as leaving the diagnostic area entirely).

There are a few more comments/suggestions I had here, but none of them are urgent or strictly necessary to fix before merging, so I think at this point I can give my approval 😄

The spacing looks off to me, it looks like each diagnostic is expecting at least 2 lines. --- Sometimes the icons look a little messed up, compare the 1st and 3rd to the second one here. Probably related to font, it only happens when hovering over some non ascii text for me. Not sure if anything can be done about it. ```gdscript func _testu(変数value, val2): pass ``` --- In light theme there is an outline for the regular doc portion, but none around the diagnostics. The diagnostic background blends into the text editor background, which doesn't happen with dark mode. This outline should probably also be around the diagnostics, though I haven't looked into why it shows. (btw I can take screen shots using print screen key and crop them after).

Tested, looks good.
Any window issues were not caused by this PR. EditorHelpBitTooltip itself is known to be implemented in a hacky way, and should be refactored in the future.
